_national.varieties: Only listed vinifera varieties (and synonyms) may be named on DO labels, e.g. Cabernet Sauvignon, Carmenère, Cot (Malbec), País, Cinsault, Carignan, Syrah, Pinot Noir, Sauvignon Blanc, Chardonnay; table-grape wine may carry no variety, vintage or quality term and must say "Vino elaborado con uva de mesa".
_national.min_alcohol: Wine at least 11.5% actual (DS 78/1986, art. 30). Since September 2026 a separate "vino bajo alcohol" category allows at least 8.5% actual without dealcoholisation (Decreto 68/2026).
_national.labelling: DO wines (Decreto 464): at least 75% from the named region, subregion, zone or area, and up to 25% from other places or varieties (no table grapes); variety 75%; vintage 75%; two or more varieties only if they make up the whole wine, named in descending order with percentages. A single-variety blend may name up to three regions or subregions in descending order, each at least 15%. Bottled in Chile. Coastal, middle and Andean complements "Costa", "Entre Cordilleras" and "Andes" need 85% from areas listed for that term. "Embotellado en Origen": own or leased vineyards and bottling plant inside the DO, made and bottled continuously by the winery. Non-DO wine may still show variety and vintage at 75%.
_national.ageing: Quality terms for DO wines (bottled in Chile, listed varieties), lowest to highest: Superior; Reserva (at least 0.5% above the legal minimum, i.e. 12.0%; oak optional); Reserva Especial (12.0% and oak); Reserva Privada (at least 1% above, i.e. 12.5%; oak optional); Gran Reserva (12.5% and oak). Alternatively: Clásico (85% from traditional varieties), Noble (botrytis, at least 16% total alcohol), Grand Cru; or Reservado, Gran Vino.
_national.sweetness: Seco up to 4 g/l (9 g/l if acidity within 2 g/l of sugar); Semi Seco up to 12 (18); Semi Dulce up to 45; Dulce 45 g/l or more. No other sweetness terms allowed.
